title: Making a top-down multiplayer shooter in Three.js where Diwali firecrackers are the weapons
author: Tall_Information_777

comments.author: aigamedev-mod
comments.body: u/Tall_Information_777 please add a bit about how you used AI and what the development process looked like. A mention that AI was involved isn't enough. It needs dev details. Rule 4 exists so promotional posts contribute to the conversation about making games. We want to avoid the sub getting drowned in low effort promotion. If this isn't updated, it may be removed.

comments.author: Tall_Information_777
comments.body:
I built ALĀTA using an AI-assisted development workflow, primarily with 
Claude Code (Opus 5.5).
The idea was a top-down multiplayer shooter visually inspired by the Dragon's Breath sequence in John Wick 4, but using Diwali firecrackers as weapons. It's actually a game concept I've dreamed of making since childhood.
Here's what went into development:

Coding: Used Claude Code to implement the game in Three.js and TypeScript. I started with the core concept, then iterated through smaller prompts to develop the weapons, physics, multiplayer and gameplay.
3D assets: Used two free textures from Polygon and generated character meshes using Tripo3D through fal.ai.
Animations: Used Mixamo for character animations.
Audio: Generated background music and sound effects using ElevenLabs.
Multiplayer: Deployed the game on Cloudflare Workers, using Durable Objects to handle multiplayer rooms.

A lot of the development involved experimentation and iteration, especially the firework effects. I wanted the sparks to look extremely sharp, bright and violent against a dark blue nighttime environment. Getting the visuals, weapon behavior and overall atmosphere to feel right took plenty of back-and-forth with the coding agent.
It's still a work in progress, but it's been satisfying to finally bring a childhood idea to life.
